name: Byron Felix
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember finding a pill bottle in a bread tin.” Friday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Byron notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I wrote his prescriptions on separate cards. Nobody wants to learn how much care is actually coming.
appearance: Byron has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for thick, tightly coiled hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an olive canvas jacket with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Byron rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Byron loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Byron remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To put a workable care schedule beside the prescriptions.
family: Isla Osei is Byron’s cousin. Byron chooses whether to use it. Isla saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *One sleeve short*, Isla says, “I wanted to sell him a full suit on credit.”
connections: Lorenzo Dixon. The old neighbor's memories put a human history beside the new prescription schedule.

reactions.response: Byron leaves the departing sibling room to get out without turning supper into a vote.
